title: Token Lifecycle Gateway: probabilistic admission, staged-model handoff, and fallback saga
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: production pods serving long-context requests occasionally hit transient GPU OOMs during busy sustained continuous-batching windows. Existing reactive eviction policies cause high tail latency and a spike in failed requests. Goal: introduce a lightweight Token Lifecycle Gateway (TLG) that sits between request admission and the continuous batching layer to reduce OOM incidents while preserving throughput and request correctness.
acceptance_criteria: TLG correctly probabilistically admits/rejects or trims tokens when headroom & KV pressure exceed thresholds
End-to-end P99 tail latency increases by <10% for non-degraded requests under same QPS compared to baseline
OOM rate reduced by >= 85% across a synthetic long-context burst workload (baseline from ENG-5023 repro)
Fallback handoff to lower-fidelity micro-models completes within configured latency budget and is logged for postmortem
Observability: per-token admission rate, KV pressure signals, and handoff counters are available in Console dashboards and can be correlated to traces
tech_notes: TLG maintains a compact in-memory token budget per request derived from GPU occupancy + hot KV size; budget calculation uses exponentially decayed moving averages to avoid oscillation
Admission policy is probabilistic: when projected occupancy > headroom threshold, accept tokens with p = headroom/projected_size to smooth flow instead of hard rejection

If admission fails for a request already partially served (mid-stream), TLG triggers a staged-model handoff: continue generation on a quantized micro-model with same tokenizer and a reconciler that rehydrates minimal KV to keep coherence

Handoff path supports three lanes: 1) prefix-trim-and-retry, 2) micro-model demotion, 3) graceful truncation with structured tool-call fallback. Lane chosen by policy ordered by quality-preservation score

Backoff & hedging: upstream caller receives a 202 with hedged-retry hints or a short-circuit response depending on SLAs; internal retries use exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaker when node-level memory pressure persists

KV operations: implement opportunistic compactors that snapshot LRU segments to host DRAM and optionally to a fast SSD tier for cold KV; compaction runs asynchronously and signals admission heuristics
GPU memory book-keeping relies on runtime hooks exposed by the allocator; we add a safe guard to treat uncertain allocator reports as high pressure to prefer conservative admission
Safety: all fallback paths preserve token-level attribution for billing/analytics and annotate outputs with provenance metadata
